verifyNote: Reference guidance. Verify laws, clauses and standards for your site and country before audit use. The official site procedure always takes priority.

activities.title: Welding and Hot Work
activities.summary: Any work that makes sparks, flame or heat that can start a fire or explosion.

where_first: Check the permit, the fire watch and the area within 11 m (35 ft) for combustibles
Look below and behind the work: floors, cracks, openings, ducts
Check cylinders, hoses, regulators and flashback arrestors
Check the extinguisher type and where it is placed
hidden_hazards: Sparks falling through gaps to lower levels
Hot slag igniting dust, oil or insulation behind walls
Fumes in enclosed areas, especially on stainless steel
Smouldering fire that starts 30 to 60 minutes after work stops
Gas hose leaks and backfire
protect_first: People working below or beside the work
A welder in a confined space or at height

elimination: Fabricate in a designated welding bay instead of in place
Use cold cutting or mechanical joining where possible
substitution: Use lower-fume processes or consumables where suitable
engineering: Local exhaust ventilation at the arc
administrative: Hot work permit and gas test
Fire watch during and after work
ppe: Helmet with correct shade, flame-resistant clothing, gloves, respirator
Welding helmet with correct shade (EN 175 / EN 379, ANSI Z87.1)
Flame-resistant welding clothing and apron (EN ISO 11611)
Respirator for the fume (EN 149 FFP3 or P100) or PAPR
permits: Gas test record where flammables may be present
checklist: Permit signed and valid for this place and time
Combustibles removed or covered within 11 m (35 ft)
Extinguisher of the right type within reach
Cylinders secured, hoses and regulators checked
Area watched for at least 30 minutes after work (many sites require 60)

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 and state rules; IS 818 (safety in electric and gas welding and cutting); BOCW Central Rules 1998 on construction sites (verify current OSH Code status)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; UAE Fire and Life Safety Code of Practice; client hot work procedures such as ADNOC and Aramco (verify)
legal.canada: CSA W117.2 (safety in welding, cutting and allied processes); provincial OHS regulations (verify province)
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Subpart Q (1910.251-.255); 29 CFR 1926 Subpart J (1926.350-.354); NFPA 51B

tbt.title: Hot work: stop sparks before they start
points: No permit, no spark
Look 11 metres around and below. If it can burn, move it or cover it
Fire watch stays at least 30 minutes after the last spark
tbt.question: What could a spark reach here that we cannot see?

activities.title: Scaffolding
activities.summary: Erecting, inspecting, using and dismantling temporary access structures.

where_first: Read the scaffold tag, inspection date and load class before climbing
Check the base: sole boards, base jacks, ground and drainage
Check bracing, ties and guardrails at every lift
Check platforms are fully boarded with toe boards and no gaps
hidden_hazards: Ties or braces removed by another trade
Ground softened by rain or digging beside the base
Platforms overloaded with stored materials
Damaged or mixed incompatible components
Gaps at ladder openings and next to the structure
protect_first: Workers below the scaffold (falling objects)
Anyone using an untagged or unfinished scaffold

elimination: Use mobile elevated work platforms or work from the ground where possible
substitution: Use system scaffold with fewer loose parts where suitable
engineering: Design by a competent person with base plates, ties, bracing, guardrails and toe boards
administrative: Only trained scaffolders erect, alter and dismantle
Inspect before first use, after weather or change, and at set intervals
Tag system: green safe, red do not use
ppe: Helmet with chin strap, harness where required, safety boots
Helmet with chin strap (EN 397 / ANSI Z89.1)
Full body harness and lanyard when erecting or dismantling (EN 361, EN 355)
permits: Permit to work at height where site rules require
checklist: Base plates and sole boards sound

legal.india: BOCW Central Rules 1998; IS 4014 (steel tubular scaffolding); Factories Act 1948 and state rules (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; Dubai Municipality and client scaffold standards; BS EN 12811 commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial OHS regulations; CSA S269.2 (access scaffolding)

tbt.title: Scaffold: read the tag before you climb
points: Green tag means inspected and safe. No tag or red tag: do not use
Never remove a tie or brace. Call the scaffolder
Keep the platform clear and within the load limit on the tag
tbt.question: Who is working under this scaffold right now?

activities.title: Confined and Enclosed Space Entry
activities.summary: Entering tanks, vessels, pits, manholes, silos, ship holds and other spaces not built for people to stay in.

where_first: Check the entry permit, isolation of pipes and power, and the rescue plan
Check atmosphere test results for oxygen, flammable and toxic gas at all levels
Check ventilation, lighting and communication with the standby
Check the way in and out and rescue equipment at the entrance
hidden_hazards: Gas layers: heavy gases sink and light gases rise, so test top, middle and bottom
Residue and sludge that release gas when disturbed
Oxygen depletion from rust, cargo or inerting
Liquids or steam entering through valves not properly isolated
Untrained rescuers who become second victims
protect_first: The person inside and the standby at the entrance
Anyone who might rush in without breathing apparatus

hazards: Toxic gas such as H2S or CO

elimination: Do the work from outside, for example by camera or robot
substitution: Use a safer cleaning method that avoids entry
engineering: Mechanical ventilation, continuous gas monitoring, safe voltage lighting, lifelines and retrieval system
administrative: Entry permit, trained attendant at all times, rescue plan with equipment and trained team, communication check
ppe: Breathing apparatus where the air is not safe, harness with lifeline, personal gas detector
Personal multi-gas detector, calibrated and bump tested
Harness with retrieval line (EN 361, EN 1496 rescue lifting device)
Breathing apparatus or airline where required (EN 137, EN 14594)
Helmet, safety boots and coverall suited to the residues
checklist: Pipes, power and moving parts isolated and locked
Atmosphere tested at all levels and within limits
Trained attendant at the entrance, entrants logged
Rescue team and equipment ready, not dependent on entry

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.36 (dangerous fumes) and state rules; BOCW Central Rules 1998 (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; ADNOC and Aramco confined space procedures; for ships IMO Resolution A.1050(27) (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial confined space regulations (for example Ontario Reg. 632/05, WorkSafeBC OHS Regulation Part 9); CSA Z1006
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 (permit-required confined spaces); 29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA; shipyards 29 CFR 1915 Subpart B; ships SOLAS and IMO A.1050(27)

tbt.title: Confined space: test before you enter, never rescue alone
points: Permit and gas test first, every time
The attendant never leaves and never goes in without breathing apparatus
If someone collapses, raise the alarm. Do not rush in
tbt.question: What is our rescue plan if the person inside collapses?

activities.title: Crane, Rigging and Lifting
activities.summary: Lifting loads with cranes, hoists and rigging gear.

where_first: Check the lift plan, load weight, radius and crane load chart
Check ground conditions and outrigger pads
Check slings, shackles and hooks: tags, wear and safe working load
Check the lift zone is barricaded and the signaller is identified
hidden_hazards: Voids or buried services under outrigger pads
Overhead power lines within reach of the boom
Wind and the surface area of the load
Hidden damage inside wire ropes and slings
Centre of gravity not where it looks
Other cranes or equipment working in the same area
protect_first: People under or near the suspended load
The signaller and rigger in the swing area

elimination: Reduce lifting by prefabricating in smaller units or using other transport
substitution: Use a larger or better placed crane instead of working near capacity
engineering: Load moment indicator, anti-two-block, exclusion zone, tag lines
administrative: Lift plan by a competent person, certified operator and rigger, daily and periodic inspection, wind limit, clear signals
ppe: Helmet, gloves, safety boots, high-visibility clothing

permits: Lift plan and critical lift permit
Crane and lifting gear inspection certificates
checklist: Lift plan approved for this load and place
Crane certificate and daily check done
Load weight known and within the load chart
Outriggers fully extended on firm pads
Slings and shackles tagged and undamaged
Safe distance from overhead lines, wind within limit

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 ss.28-29 (hoists, lifts and lifting machines); BOCW Central Rules 1998; IS 3177 (EOT cranes) (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client lifting standards; BS 7121 commonly used (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z150 (mobile cranes) and provincial OHS regulations
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC (cranes and derricks in construction); 29 CFR 1910.179 and 1910.184 (overhead cranes, slings)

tbt.title: Lifting: nobody stands under a load
points: Check the tag and the load weight before the hook goes on
Only the signaller gives signals. Anyone can shout stop
Keep out of the swing and fall zone
tbt.question: If this load slipped now, where would it land?

activities.title: Excavation and Trenching

where_first: Check utility drawings and scan results before any dig
Check soil type, water and nearby loads or vibration
Check edge protection and a way out within reach of workers
Check shoring or sloping matches the depth and soil
hidden_hazards: Live cables, gas and water lines not on drawings
Water seeping in after rain and undermining the wall
Spoil heaps and equipment too close to the edge
Previously disturbed soil that is weaker
Toxic or oxygen-poor air in deeper trenches
protect_first: Workers inside the trench
People and vehicles near the edge

substitution: Use shorter open lengths and backfill promptly
engineering: Edge barriers and ladders or ramps so no worker has more than 7.5 m (25 ft) to travel to exit
administrative: Competent person inspects daily and after rain
Permit to dig and utility locate
Keep spoil and equipment at least 0.6 m (2 ft) from the edge

ppe: Gas detector for deep or suspect trenches
checklist: Protective system in place for trenches 1.5 m (5 ft) or deeper unless in stable rock
Edge protection and spoil set back
Atmosphere tested if deep or near contamination

legal.india: BOCW Central Rules 1998; IS 3764 (excavation work code of safety) (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; utility authority approvals and client permit to dig (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial construction regulations (for example WorkSafeBC OHS Regulation Part 20, Ontario Reg. 213/91)

tbt.title: Trench: never work in an unprotected trench
points: Scan and permit before the first dig
Shoring or sloping before anyone goes in
Keep spoil and machines back from the edge
tbt.question: What is holding the wall up where we are standing?

activities.title: Working at Height
activities.summary: Any work where a person could fall and be injured: roofs, ladders, platforms, edges, openings.

where_first: Check the method: can the work be done from the ground or a platform?
Check anchor points are rated and edge protection is complete
Check the harness, lanyard and rescue plan
Check the surface: fragile roof, wet or loose material
hidden_hazards: Fragile roof sheets and skylights hidden by paint or dirt
Anchors that look strong but are not rated
Suspension trauma if a fallen worker cannot be rescued fast
Unprotected openings and edges around the work
Swing fall when the anchor is not overhead
protect_first: Workers near an unprotected edge
People below the work area

elimination: Do the work at ground level or by prefabrication
substitution: Use a platform or MEWP instead of a ladder
engineering: Guardrails, covers on openings, safety nets, rated anchor points, tool lanyards
administrative: Permit, trained workers, rescue plan, inspect equipment before use, barricade below
ppe: Full body harness with shock absorber on a rated anchor
Full body harness (EN 361) with energy absorber (EN 355)
checklist: Rescue plan and trained rescuers ready
Protection starts at 1.8 m (6 ft) in US construction and 1.2 m (4 ft) in US general industry; other countries set their own height

legal.india: BOCW Central Rules 1998; Factories Act 1948 and state rules; IS 3521 (industrial safety belts and harnesses) (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client standards; EN 363 fall protection systems commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z259 series (fall protection) and provincial OHS regulations, which set the height trigger
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart M (1926.501); 29 CFR 1910 Subpart D (1910.28)

tbt.title: Height: clip on before you step out
points: Check your harness and anchor every time
Never walk on a roof sheet unless it is proven safe
Keep tools tied so they cannot fall on others
tbt.question: If I fell now, who would reach me and how fast?

typical: No harness or not clipped on

activities.title: Electrical Work and Energy Isolation
activities.summary: Working on or near electrical equipment and isolating all energy before maintenance.

where_first: Confirm who is qualified and authorised for this work
Check isolation points and a lock and tag on every energy source
Test for dead with a proven tester before touching (test, prove, test)
Check arc flash and shock boundaries and PPE category
hidden_hazards: Back-feed from generators, UPS and solar
Stored energy in capacitors, springs and hydraulics
Wrong circuit isolated because panels are not labelled
Damaged tools and leads with cracked insulation
Wet conditions that change the risk
protect_first: The person working on the equipment
Others who might switch it on

substitution: Use lower voltage or battery tools
engineering: RCD / GFCI protection, insulated tools, barriers and covers, interlocked doors
administrative: Lockout tagout with personal locks, permit, authorised persons only, test-prove-test, arc flash labels
ppe: Arc-rated clothing and face shield, insulated gloves, rated tools
Arc-rated clothing and face shield (IEC 61482-2, NFPA 70E)
Insulating gloves with leather protectors (IEC 60903, ASTM D120)
Dielectric safety boots (EN ISO 20345 or ASTM F2413 EH)
checklist: All energy sources identified and isolated
Personal lock and tag on every isolation point
Tested dead with a tester proved before and after
Arc flash boundary and PPE checked

legal.india: CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations; Indian Electricity Rules 1956 where applicable (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; local utility regulations (DEWA, SEWA, Kahramaa, SEC) and client LOTO standards (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z460 (control of hazardous energy) and CSA Z462 (workplace electrical safety); provincial regulations
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 (LOTO), 1910.333 (work practices), 1910 Subpart S; 1926 Subpart K; NFPA 70E

tbt.title: Electrical: lock it, tag it, test it, then touch it
points: Every person puts on their own lock
Test the tester, test the circuit, test the tester again
If you did not isolate it, treat it as live
tbt.question: How do we know this circuit is really dead?

activities.title: Chemical and SDS Handling
activities.summary: Storing, using, decanting and disposing of hazardous chemicals.

where_first: Check the label and SDS for every chemical in use
Check storage: segregation, bunding, ventilation and labels
Check the spill kit, eyewash and shower are within reach and working
Check decanted containers are labelled
hidden_hazards: Incompatible chemicals stored together (acids with bases, oxidisers with fuels)
Unlabelled decanted bottles
Vapours collecting in low areas or closed rooms
Expired or damaged containers leaking at the back of the store
Eyewash stations that are blocked or dry
protect_first: The person with contact, splash or inhalation
Workers downwind in poorly ventilated areas

elimination: Remove the chemical or process step if not needed
engineering: Local exhaust, closed transfer, bunded storage, segregated cabinets
administrative: SDS in a language workers understand, training, labelling, inventory, spill procedure
ppe: Gloves and goggles matched to the chemical, apron, respirator where needed
Chemical-resistant gloves chosen from the SDS (EN 374)
Chemical-resistant apron or suit (EN 943 for severe hazards)
Respirator with correct filter (EN 14387 gas filters, EN 149 particle)
Safety boots with chemical resistance (EN ISO 20345)
permits: Hot work or hazardous area permit where flammable

legal.india: MSIHC Rules 1989; Factories Act 1948 Chapter IVA (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; GHS labelling and SDS; local authority chemical control rules (verify)
legal.canada: WHMIS 2015 under the Hazardous Products Act and Hazardous Products Regulations; provincial OHS
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 (Hazard Communication, GHS); 29 CFR 1910 Subpart Z

tbt.title: Chemicals: read the label before you open it
points: If the bottle has no label, do not use it
Never mix chemicals. Acid and chlorine make toxic gas
Know where the eyewash is before you start
tbt.question: What would we do in the first minute of a splash in the eyes?

activities.title: Forklift and Material Handling Equipment
activities.summary: Operating forklifts, pallet trucks and other powered handling equipment.

where_first: Check the daily inspection: brakes, steering, horn, lights, forks, mast, chains, tyres
Check the route: ramps, blind corners, doors and pedestrian crossings
Check the operator's licence or authorisation
Check the load rating plate and that the seat belt works
hidden_hazards: Blind spots when reversing with a high load
Pedestrians stepping out of racking aisles
Damaged, wet or sloped floors
Battery charging areas where hydrogen collects
Forks left raised or trucks left unattended
protect_first: Pedestrians near travel routes
The operator in a tip-over (seat belt on)

hazards: Exhaust fumes from LPG or diesel trucks indoors

elimination: Change the layout to remove truck movement through pedestrian areas
substitution: Use pallet trucks for short moves
engineering: Segregated walkways, mirrors, blue spot lights, speed limiters, proximity sensors, seat belts
administrative: Trained and authorised operators, one-way traffic, speed limits, daily checks, banksman at blind areas
ppe: Safety boots, high-visibility clothing, helmet where overhead risk

checklist: Operator authorised and wearing the seat belt
Daily check done and defects reported
Forks low when travelling, load stable
Horn works and speed limit followed
Trucks parked with forks down and key out

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 and state rules; Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for road use (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client MHE and operator authorisation rules (verify)
legal.canada: CSA B335 (lift trucks) and provincial regulations

tbt.title: Forklift: eyes first, then wheels
points: Stop and look at every blind corner
Pedestrians always have right of way
Forks down, key out when you leave the truck
tbt.question: Where are the blind spots on our busiest route?

activities.title: Grinding and Cutting
activities.summary: Using angle grinders, abrasive wheels and cutting discs.

where_first: Check the disc is the right type and size, in date and undamaged
Check the guard is fitted and adjusted
Check the disc speed rating is at or above the tool speed
Check spark direction and nearby combustibles
hidden_hazards: Cracked discs that have been dropped
Wrong disc for the job (cutting disc used for grinding)
Guards removed to reach tight spaces
Dust from silica, metal or paint
Kickback when the disc binds
protect_first: The operator's face, eyes and hands
People within the spark and fragment zone

elimination: Use cold cutting or prefabrication where possible
substitution: Use shears or saws that make less dust
engineering: Fixed guards, dead-man switch, dust extraction, clamps to hold work
administrative: Inspect and ring test discs, trained users, tool tagging, hot work permit where required, limit exposure time
ppe: Face shield over glasses, gloves, hearing and dust protection
Face shield over safety glasses (EN 166 / ANSI Z87.1)
Respirator for dust (EN 149 FFP2 or FFP3)
Flame-resistant clothing for heavy spark work (EN ISO 11612)
permits: Hot work permit where sparks can ignite
checklist: Disc suitable, undamaged and in date

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 ss.21-22 (machinery safety) and the relevant IS code for abrasive wheels (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN 12413 for bonded abrasive products commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z432 (safeguarding of machinery) and provincial regulations
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.215 (abrasive wheel machinery) and 1910.243 (portable tools)

tbt.title: Grinder: guard on, shield on, eyes first
points: Never remove the guard
Check the disc for cracks every time. If dropped, bin it
Hold with two hands and stand out of the line of the disc
tbt.question: What happens to my face if this disc breaks?

activities.title: Pressure Testing
activities.summary: Testing pipes, vessels and systems under pressure with liquid or gas.

where_first: Check the approved test procedure, test pressure, medium and who approved it
Check the test boundary: blinds, isolation, drains and vents
Check gauges are calibrated and the relief device is set
Check the exclusion zone and warning signs
hidden_hazards: Trapped air in a hydro test which makes failure far more violent
Components not rated for the test pressure
Flange or thread leaks at the test boundary
Temperature changes raising pressure in a closed system
Untested temporary hoses and fittings
protect_first: People inside the exclusion zone
The test crew near connections while pressurising

elimination: Use alternative verification where the code permits
substitution: Use liquid (hydro) testing instead of pneumatic where practicable
engineering: Barriers, relief valves, remote pressurising, restraints on hoses
administrative: Approved procedure and permit, competent supervisor, staged pressure increase with hold points, exclusion zone, no work on connections under pressure

checklist: All components rated for the test pressure
Air vented from a liquid test
Pressure raised in stages with hold points

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.31 (pressure plant); Indian Boilers Act 1923 where applicable (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client pressure testing standards; ASME B31.3 and PCC-2 commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial pressure equipment regulations (for example TSSA in Ontario, Technical Safety BC); CSA B51
legal.usa: ASME B31.3 and PCC-2; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 for energy control; General Duty Clause

tbt.title: Pressure test: respect the stored energy
points: Nobody tightens or touches a connection under pressure
Keep out of the barrier zone during the test
Vent the air out of a hydro test first
tbt.question: What is the worst thing that fails at this pressure and where does it go?
